cues.caption: Welcome back, champ!
cues.text: Hey champ, welcome back! I'm so happy to see you again.

cues.caption: Last time: labels must be right
cues.text: Last time, we played show and tell with labels. A label is the name we stick on an example, like apple. And we saw that wrong labels teach wrong things!

cues.caption: Chapter 4 · Data — The Food AI Eats
cues.text: Today is chapter four of How Machines Learn. It's called, Data, the food AI eats!

cues.caption: AI eats food?! Let's find out.
cues.text: Wait. AI eats food? Does it munch on samosas? Hmm. Not quite! Let's find out what AI really eats.

cues.caption: Meet Meera and her puppy, Bruno
cues.text: Meet Meera. She's ten years old, and she loves dogs. Her puppy Bruno is small, brown, and very naughty.

cues.caption: Dog Spotter learns from 500 photos of Bruno
cues.text: For her science fair, Meera makes a little AI app called Dog Spotter. She shows it five hundred photos. All of them are Bruno, labelled dog.

cues.caption: Big, white Moti → "Not a dog!"
cues.text: The next day, Moti walks past her gate. Moti is the big, white street dog everyone loves. Meera points her tablet at him. And Dog Spotter says, not a dog!

cues.caption: Why did the app get it wrong? Think!
cues.text: Huh? Moti is clearly a dog! Why do you think the app got it wrong? Think about it.

cues.caption: Hold that thought…
cues.text: Hold that thought. We'll come back to Meera very soon. First, we need one important word.

cues.caption: DATA = information AI learns from
cues.text: That word is data. Data is the information AI learns from. Pictures, words, sounds, and even numbers.

cues.caption: Data is the food AI eats
cues.text: You can think of data as the food AI eats. You need food to grow strong. And AI needs data to learn. No data, no learning!

cues.caption: Dataset = a big collection of data
cues.text: When we put lots of data together, like one thousand dog photos, we call it a dataset. A dataset is a big collection of data.

cues.caption: Pictures: cats, mangoes, buses
cues.text: So, what's on AI's menu? First, pictures. Photos of cats, mangoes, buses, anything!

cues.caption: Words: stories, messages, questions
cues.text: Next, words. Stories, messages, and questions that people type.

cues.caption: Sounds: voices, songs, barking
cues.text: And sounds! Voices, songs, even a dog barking. A voice assistant learned to understand people by listening to lots and lots of voices.

cues.caption: Real shoes: not data. A photo of shoes: data!
cues.text: But careful. A real glass of water, or a real pair of shoes, is not data. A photo of your shoes? That's data! AI learns from information, not from real things.

cues.caption: Only rice, every single day? Hmm…
cues.text: Now, think about your own food. What if you ate only rice? Rice for breakfast, rice for lunch, rice for dinner. Every single day!

cues.caption: A thali: dal, sabzi, roti, curd, fruit
cues.text: You'd miss so much! A good thali has dal, sabzi, roti, curd, and fruit. Different foods help you grow strong. Yum.

cues.caption: Variety = many different kinds
cues.text: AI is just the same. It learns best from variety. Variety means many different kinds, not just one kind, again and again.

cues.caption: Only Bruno → it thinks dog = small & brown
cues.text: Now, remember Meera's Dog Spotter? It only ever saw Bruno. Small, and brown. So what did it learn? That a dog means small and brown!

cues.caption: Moti didn't match anything it had seen
cues.text: So when big, white Moti came along, the app was confused. It had never seen a dog like him.

cues.caption: Big · small · brown · white · spotty dogs
cues.text: So Meera adds variety. Big dogs, small dogs. Brown, white, black, and spotty dogs. Hundreds of different dogs!

cues.caption: Now it spots Moti! Variety works.
cues.text: Now the app finds what all dogs share. Four legs, a tail, a furry body, and a wet nose. And this time, it spots Moti right away! Woof!

cues.caption: Which dataset teaches "dog" best?
cues.text: Your turn! Which dataset would teach AI dog the best? A, five hundred photos of only brown puppies. B, just one photo of a dog. Or C, five hundred photos of big, small, brown, white, and spotty dogs. Pause, and think.

cues.caption: C! Lots of photos AND lots of variety
cues.text: It's C! Lots of photos, and lots of variety. A shows only one kind of dog, and B is far too little. One photo can't teach a whole idea.

cues.caption: Some data should stay private
cues.text: Now, here's something very important. Not all data should be collected. Some data is private.

cues.caption: Public: trees, animals, the Taj Mahal
cues.text: Public data is okay to share. Pictures of trees, animals, or famous buildings, like the Taj Mahal.

cues.caption: Private: address, phone number, family photos
cues.text: Private data is about a person, and it should stay safe. Like your home address, your phone number, and your family photos.

cues.caption: No collecting private data without permission!
cues.text: So, what if an app quietly collects everyone's family photos, without asking? That's not okay! Private data should not be collected without permission.

cues.caption: Public or private? Sort them!
cues.text: Quick game! Public, or private? A photo of a tree. Your home address. A picture of the Taj Mahal. Your phone number. Pause, and sort them.

cues.caption: Tree, Taj Mahal: public. Address, phone: private
cues.text: The tree and the Taj Mahal are public. Your address and your phone number are private. Keep those safe, champ!

cues.caption: Your turn: practice check
cues.text: Okay champ, here's your practice check, just like the quiz.

cues.caption: 200 photos of only parrots: enough? Why?
cues.text: An AI needs to learn bird. Is two hundred photos of only parrots enough? Why, or why not? Pause the video, and try it on paper.

cues.caption: No! It needs crows, sparrows, pigeons, peacocks…
cues.text: Here's one answer. No, it's not enough! The AI might think only parrots are birds. Then it sees a crow, and says, not a bird! It needs many kinds, like crows, sparrows, pigeons, and peacocks, to learn what all birds share. Brilliant!

cues.caption: Data is the food AI eats
cues.text: Let's remember what we learned. Data is the food AI eats.

cues.caption: Pictures, words & sounds are data
cues.text: Pictures, words, and sounds are all data.

cues.caption: Variety teaches AI better
cues.text: Varied data, with many different kinds, teaches AI better.

cues.caption: Some data should stay private
cues.text: And some data, like your home address, should stay private.

cues.caption: Chapter 4 done!
cues.text: Chapter four, done! Now you know what AI eats, champ. Just one more chapter in this unit!

cues.text: Now let's see what you remember. Tap Finish, and try the quiz. You've got this!
